question.problem:
The weights of some chocolate cookies are normally distributed with a mean of $10\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $1\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$ The weights of some oatcakes are normally distributed with a mean of $15\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $2\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$  If one chocolate cookie and one oatcake are randomly selected, what is the probability that $6$ times the weight of the cookie plus $4$ times the weight of oatcake is less than $120\,\text{g}$, but more than $100\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights of the cookies and oatcakes are independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-2.5\,$ | $\,0.0062\,$ | $\,0.0060\,$ | $\,0.0059\,$ | $\,0.0057\,$ | $\,0.0055\,$ |
| $\,-2.4\,$ | $\,0.0082\,$ | $\,0.0080\,$ | $\,0.0078\,$ | $\,0.0075\,$ | $\,0.0073\,$ |
| $\,-2.3\,$ | $\,0.0107\,$ | $\,0.0104\,$ | $\,0.0102\,$ | $\,0.0099\,$ | $\,0.0096\,$ |
